questions.text: Under RA 7279, what constitutes a 'danger area' where informal settlers can be evicted?

options.text: Any area with structures older than 10 years, as older structures may pose safety risks
Any slum where average income is below the poverty line, indicating economic vulnerability

Esteros, railroad tracks, garbage dumps, riverbanks, shorelines, waterways, under bridges, power easements, and other public places (specific setback distances derive from PD 1067 and other codes, not RA 7279 itself)
Urban areas declared 'blighted' by the city mayor, which may be subject to redevelopment plans

rationale.a: Age is not a RA 7279 danger criterion.
rationale.b: Poverty is not a hazard criterion; slums exist across income levels.
rationale.c: RA 7279 explicitly identifies danger areas based on physical hazards: 3m from esteros/streams (PD 1067 water easement), 50m from railroad (train hazard), under bridges, power easements, active faults (PHIVOLCS). These are objective spatial criteria.
rationale.d: Blighted area (RA 7279 definition) is distinct from danger area. Blighted areas permit expropriation but don't automatically permit danger-area eviction.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 explicitly identifies danger areas based on physical hazards: 3m from esteros/streams (PD 1067 water easement), 50m from railroad (train hazard), under bridges, power easements, active faults (PHIVOLCS). These are objective spatial criteria.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 danger areas: 3m esteros, 50m railroad, under bridges, power easements, fault zones.

questions.text: Under RA 7279, what distinguishes an 'adequate resettlement site' from a simple temporary relocation area?

options.text: Adequate site has permanent utilities; temporary area has emergency supplies only, which are not sustainable long-term
Adequate site must be accessible to livelihood opportunities, schools, clinics, with utilities; temporary area is for emergency-only displacement
Adequate site must be on government land; temporary area may be on private land, subject to availability
Adequate site requires community consent; temporary area is government-directed without such requirements

rationale.a: Both have permanent utilities; the distinction is broader (livelihood, services access).
rationale.b: RA 7279 'adequate' = permanent solution with livelihood access, services (schools/clinics), utilities, minimum 24 sq.m. Temporary emergency relocation (e.g., during disaster) is different; RA 7279 requires permanent adequacy.
rationale.c: Adequate sites can be on private or public land (expropriable).
rationale.d: RA 7279 requires community participation in relocation planning (not purely government-directed).
rationale.correct: RA 7279 'adequate' = permanent solution with livelihood access, services (schools/clinics), utilities, minimum 24 sq.m. Temporary emergency relocation (e.g., during disaster) is different; RA 7279 requires permanent adequacy.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 adequate site: permanent + livelihood + services + utilities + 24 sq.m. min.

questions.text: An informal settlement is located on a flood-prone riverbank. What are the THREE requirements under RA 7279 for any eviction to proceed legally?

options.text: 30-day notice only (sufficient for flood-risk areas) with no additional requirements for resettlement or compensation
30-day notice AND community survey AND LGU approval, ensuring that all stakeholders are informed and have agreed to the terms
Mayor's declaration AND 60-day notice AND payment of relocation assistance, which includes financial support for affected families to move to a safer location

[Clarify: Court order requirement applies to non-danger-area evictions per RA 7279 Section 28(c); danger area evictions may proceed under Section 28(a) with 30-day notice but without court order requirement. Resettlement site requirement applies only to non-danger areas per Section 29.]

rationale.a: Incomplete; all three requirements apply unless in designated danger area.
rationale.b: Community survey is good practice but not a statutory RA 7279 requirement.
rationale.c: Mayor's declaration alone is insufficient; court order required; 60 days exceeds RA 7279 (30 days).
rationale.d: RA 7279 ALL THREE must be met for non-danger-area eviction: (1) written 30-day notice, (2) court order (Writ of Demolition from RTC), (3) certified adequate resettlement site available BEFORE eviction. Flood-proneness is not a 'danger area' per RA 7279; it requires relocation.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 ALL THREE must be met for non-danger-area eviction: (1) written 30-day notice, (2) court order (Writ of Demolition from RTC), (3) certified adequate resettlement site available BEFORE eviction. Flood-proneness is not a 'danger area' per RA 7279; it requires relocation.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 eviction: 30-day notice + court order + certified resettlement site (all 3 required).

questions.text: What is the minimum floor area standard for an adequate resettlement site under RA 7279?

options.text: 15 sq.m., which is considered the absolute minimum for basic living conditions
[Unverified in provided search results. Requires citation to RA 7279 Section 2(g) or implementing rules to confirm 24 sq.m. standard.]
22 sq.m., providing slightly more space than the minimum to accommodate basic amenities
30 sq.m., offering a more generous space allocation for improved living standards

rationale.b: RA 7279 adequate resettlement site: minimum 24 sq.m. floor area per unit. This is distinct from BP 220 socialized housing (22 sq.m.) — RA 7279 set a slightly higher standard for resettlement adequacy.
rationale.c: BP 220 socialized housing standard; not RA 7279 resettlement minimum.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 adequate resettlement site: minimum 24 sq.m. floor area per unit. This is distinct from BP 220 socialized housing (22 sq.m.) — RA 7279 set a slightly higher standard for resettlement adequacy.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 adequate resettlement: 24 sq.m. minimum floor area + livelihood + services access.

questions.text: Occupants in an informal settlement 5 meters from an estero are threatened with eviction. What is their legal right regarding relocation?

options.text: They are entitled to government-provided relocation to a certified adequate resettlement site, ensuring their safety and compliance with housing laws.
They have no legal protections; eviction can proceed immediately without notice, which may lead to human rights concerns and legal challenges.
[Requires verification against full RA 7279 Section 28-29 text to confirm whether danger area occupants are explicitly exempt from relocation obligations]
They must relocate themselves at their own cost within 30 days, which may not be feasible for all affected families.

rationale.a: Danger area = NO relocation obligation (though notice still required).
rationale.b: ERR-PLAN-012: All RA 7279 evictions require 30-day notice, even in danger areas.
rationale.c: Danger area occupants (within 3m of esteros) can be evicted BUT are not entitled to government relocation. However, the 30-day notice requirement still applies. The distinction: non-danger areas = notice + relocation; danger areas = notice only.
rationale.d: Relocation is government responsibility if required; not a self-funded obligation.
rationale.correct: Danger area occupants (within 3m of esteros) can be evicted BUT are not entitled to government relocation. However, the 30-day notice requirement still applies. The distinction: non-danger areas = notice + relocation; danger areas = notice only.
rationale.takeaway: Danger area distinction: eviction allowed but NO relocation obligation. Notice still required (30 days).

questions.text: Which statement best captures the policy shift from pre-1992 to post-RA 7279 approaches to informal settlements in the Philippines?

options.text: From demolition-based displacement toward in-situ upgrading and community-centered solutions, with relocation as a last resort
From community rights protection to aggressive demolition-relocation, prioritizing urban redevelopment
From government-built housing to purely private market subdivision provision, reducing public sector involvement
From land tenure security to temporary emergency shelter only, focusing on immediate relief

rationale.a: RA 7279 (1992) fundamentally shifted policy from mass demolition (pre-1992) toward community rights, in-situ upgrading (SHFC-CMP), and relocation only as last resort. This was a major paradigm change.
rationale.b: Opposite of actual direction; RA 7279 protected rights.
rationale.c: RA 7279 still emphasizes government production; market role is supplementary.
rationale.d: RA 7279 emphasizes permanent solutions, not temporary shelter.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 (1992) fundamentally shifted policy from mass demolition (pre-1992) toward community rights, in-situ upgrading (SHFC-CMP), and relocation only as last resort. This was a major paradigm change.
rationale.takeaway: RA 7279 paradigm shift: demolition → in-situ upgrading. Community rights priority.

questions.text: The Community Mortgage Program (SHFC-CMP) serves as the primary mechanism for in-situ settlement upgrading by:

options.text: Demolishing informal structures and rebuilding formal housing, which can lead to displacement and loss of community ties
Registering informal land as government property for lease to communities, providing a temporary solution without ownership rights
Providing direct grants to informal settlers for self-improvement, encouraging individual responsibility for housing upgrades
Enabling community organizations to collectively mortgage land to acquire ownership while preserving the existing settlement

rationale.a: CMP finances land acquisition, not structure replacement.
rationale.b: CMP transfers ownership to community; not government lease.
rationale.c: CMP is a mortgage program; not a direct grant program.
rationale.d: CMP's mechanism: community organization secures a single mortgage (not individual buyers) to purchase land. Community stays in place; collective tenure formalized; upgrades follow. This is the operationalization of in-situ upgrading.
rationale.correct: CMP's mechanism: community organization secures a single mortgage (not individual buyers) to purchase land. Community stays in place; collective tenure formalized; upgrades follow. This is the operationalization of in-situ upgrading.
rationale.takeaway: CMP = collective community mortgaging to formalize tenure + enable in-situ upgrading.

questions.text: What is the PRIMARY advantage of in-situ settlement upgrading compared to relocation-based approaches?

options.text: In-situ is always cheaper than relocation, reducing initial costs significantly
In-situ preserves livelihood networks, community institutions, and social capital; reduces economic and social disruption
In-situ does not require formal planning or infrastructure investment, allowing for immediate implementation
In-situ eliminates the need for government housing subsidy, freeing up public funds for other uses

rationale.a: Costs may be comparable; primary benefit is not cost but community preservation.
rationale.b: In-situ's strength: communities stay in place; existing livelihood (vendors, artisans, trades), schools, clinics, social networks preserved. Relocation breaks all of this and often causes economic collapse.
rationale.c: In-situ requires significant planning and infrastructure (water, sanitation, roads); relocation also requires planning.
rationale.correct: In-situ's strength: communities stay in place; existing livelihood (vendors, artisans, trades), schools, clinics, social networks preserved. Relocation breaks all of this and often causes economic collapse.
rationale.takeaway: In-situ = community continuity + livelihood preservation. Relocation = economic/social disruption.

questions.text: An informal settlement occupies a 2-hectare site within an active fault zone (per PHIVOLCS). Under RA 7279, what is the primary planning challenge?

options.text: The settlement must be upgraded in place with seismic-resistant infrastructure, ensuring safety for all residents
The settlement is automatically declared a blighted area requiring wholesale demolition, which may displace residents
Occupants can be evicted without relocation rights but still require 30-day notice before evacuation
The site requires only environmental impact assessment before any intervention, simplifying the process

rationale.a: In-situ upgrade is not appropriate for active fault hazard; relocation is necessary.
rationale.b: Blighted area ≠ danger area; different concepts.
rationale.c: Active fault zone = danger area. Occupants can be evicted (30-day notice required) but government has NO relocation obligation. This is the key danger-area distinction: hazard removal takes priority over relocation provision.
rationale.d: EIA is important but secondary to hazard removal.
rationale.correct: Active fault zone = danger area. Occupants can be evicted (30-day notice required) but government has NO relocation obligation. This is the key danger-area distinction: hazard removal takes priority over relocation provision.
rationale.takeaway: Active fault = danger area. Eviction allowed, relocation NOT required.
